title: Singapore Companies' Efforts to Upskill Employees and Use of SkillsFuture Credits to Train for Alternative Careers
what_it_is: Singapore Companies' Efforts to Upskill Employees and Use of SkillsFuture Credits to Train for Alternative Careers

sections.label: Training subsidies and participation rates
sections.summary: MOE and SSG provide about $400 million yearly in training subsidies, with 62% of employed Singaporeans in structured training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, the Ministry of Education (MOE) and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) provide about $400 million a year in direct training subsidies for lifelong learning, with as much as 40% of that going towards supporting individual-initiated training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Sixty percent, the majority, still goes towards supporting companies and employers to train their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Employed Singaporeans' participation rate in structured training is now 62%, higher than the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development average of 55%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Further, based on our surveys in 2014, 82% of surveyed employers provided structured training to their employees, compared to 72% in 2006.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit utilisation
sections.summary: As at end December 2016, over 126,000 Singapore Citizens used $37 million of their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We track the utilisation closely and the latest results were just released yesterday and carried widely in the papers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, as at end December 2016, over 126,000 Singapore Citizens have utilised $37 million worth of their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: Skills Development Levy and prioritisation
sections.summary: Companies set aside 0.25% of payroll under the Skills Development Levy, and efforts should prioritise sectors and companies hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Under Skills Development Levy, every company sets aside 0.25% of their payroll for workers up to $4,500 in salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, in a way, that mechanism is in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is levied very lightly at 0.25% but we will be very careful not to add a further burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What  we should really do is what the Member suggested in her second question − prioritise where the economic activities are, which sectors, which companies are hiring and then put very focused efforts to help workers pick up the skills so that they can take up the new jobs.
